cover.headline: A coal-tar champion priced as a battery-materials company: the profits have not caught up with the price
cover.lead: Himadri turns coal tar, a by-product of steel-making, into pitch for aluminium smelters and graphite electrodes, carbon black for tyres and plastics, naphthalene and speciality oils. It is India's largest pitch maker (65%+ share) and has quadrupled its EBITDA per tonne since FY22, taking net profit from ₹39 cr to ₹755 cr. Now it is spending ~₹2,000 cr on battery materials (LFP cathode, anode), carbon nanotubes and a revived tyre brand (Birla Tyres). The only institutional broker, ICICI Securities, values it on a sum of the parts with the core on EV/EBITDA; we use **P/E: 25x Sep-28E EPS of ₹20.9** (its own forward median since 2021), which gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**, so **we initiate with SELL.** EV/EBITDA (₹489) agrees; the DCF (₹330) is lower still. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The core business has been transformed
arguments.p: EBITDA per tonne rose from ~₹4,400 (FY22) to ₹17,331 (FY26) and ~₹23,654 in Q1FY27, on speciality carbon black (now 130 kt), better pitch grades and cost control. ROE is ~18% and the company is net cash. This is a well-run, integrated business.

arguments.h: But growth was margin, not volume, and margins can turn
arguments.p: Revenue was flat from FY23 to FY26 and volume grew 2% in FY26; Q1FY27 volume fell 6% while prices rose 23% on costlier raw materials. We assume EBITDA per tonne eases to ~₹20,500 in FY27. The new capacity (pitch exports, anthraquinone, SSCB, CNT) is real but small next to a ₹4,400 cr core.

arguments.h: The new bets are early and capital-hungry
arguments.p: LFP (₹1,125 cr) starts with a 2,000 t plant in Q3FY27 and has no disclosed orders; the company prices at par with China. Tyres absorbed ~₹490 cr of NCD funding for ₹187 cr of FY26 revenue at break-even. Free cash flow turns negative in FY27-28E on our numbers, and ROE dips to ~16%.

arguments.h: The price already pays for success
arguments.p: At ₹678 the stock trades at 35.2x our FY28E EPS and 42.9x trailing (five-year median 39.1x), while listed chemical peers trade a median 28% below their medians. Valuing the core at 16x EBITDA, the market implies ~₹10,400 cr for battery materials that have yet to sell.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether volume returns (management promised growth "from both volume and value") and whether EBITDA per tonne holds near Q1's ~₹23,700.
LFP: commissioning of the 2,000 tpa plant (Q3FY27) and the first customer approvals (sample stages C and D); any disclosed offtake.
Anode: announcement of a commercial-scale plant and its capex; Sicona and IBC milestones (IBC's India gigafactory targeted for Q4FY27).
Birla Tyres: EBITDA break-even in FY27 as guided; approvals for the scheme to demerge DBRL's tyre business into HSCL.
Anthraquinone/carbazole Phase 1 (Q2FY27), CNT (Q4FY27); liquid pitch export volumes.
Management's FY28 target of ₹1,100 cr+ PAT: we are at ~₹{{F.pat.1|num}} cr.

sections.title: One coal-tar chain, three businesses

blocks.p: Coal tar is a sticky by-product of the coke ovens that feed steel blast furnaces. Himadri buys it from steel makers and importers and distils it (600,000 tpa; the largest single-location complex in the world, per the company). About half becomes **coal tar pitch**, the binder in the carbon anodes of aluminium smelters and in graphite electrodes. The lighter fractions become **naphthalene** (for phthalic anhydride, SNF concrete admixtures and mothballs) and **speciality oils**, which also feed its own **carbon black** plants (tyres and rubber, plus speciality grades for plastics, inks, cables and batteries). A captive power plant runs on carbon-black tail gas. Exports were 29% of FY26 revenue (61 countries). On top of this core sit two new businesses: **Birla Tyres** (restarted in May-2025) and **new energy materials** (LFP cathode and anode for lithium-ion batteries).

Bain Capital, the only large outside investor (₹413 cr in 2009-10), sold out in FY2021-22.

sections.title: Coal tar is a by-product business; carbon black and batteries are global commodities

blocks.p: Coal tar supply is set by steel-making, not by demand for pitch: every tonne of metallurgical coke yields a few per cent of tar, so supply grows with India's blast-furnace steel output and imports fill the gap. Demand comes from three places. **Aluminium smelters** need pitch to bind their carbon anodes (India is adding smelter and refinery capacity). **Graphite electrodes** for electric-arc steel use pitch as binder and impregnant (an oversupplied industry: HEG and Graphite India earned 3-7% ROE in FY26). **Carbon black** for tyres is a ~15 mn t global market growing ~2-3% a year, of which speciality grades (~1.1 mn t) grow ~4% (Notch Consulting via the annual report). Battery materials are a different world: China makes essentially all LFP cathode and most anode material, and cell-component prices fell 50-60% in 4-5 years.

sections.title: Carbon materials & chemicals: the cash engine, now priced off higher raw-material costs

pair.title: Core revenue: flat for three years, +15% in Q1FY27
pair.unit: Carbon materials & chemicals incl. power, external (₹ crore)

pair.title: Segment EBIT margin: 13% to 21%
pair.source: Quarterly segment results (Q2FY26 restated split derived)

bullets: **What drives it.** Volume (capacity ~80% used in Q1FY27, 90%+ expected in FY27) times realisation (raw-material costs are passed on with a lag) times the mix of higher-value products. The company does not disclose product-wise volumes or prices, so we cannot split pitch from carbon black or oils.

**Q1FY27.** Standalone volume 131,844 t (-6% YoY) but revenue +16%: coal tar and oil prices rose after the April-May West Asia crisis and Himadri passed them on. Standalone EBITDA per tonne was ~₹22,900, up from ~₹16,700 a year ago and ~₹18,600 in Q4FY26. Management says the margins are "sustainable" and denies inventory gains.

**New capacity.** Distillation debottlenecked from 500 kt to 600 kt; liquid pitch terminals at Haldia and Mangalore; anthraquinone and carbazole (2,600 tpa in Q2FY27, 5,300 tpa by Q2FY28, ₹248 cr capex); CNT 200 tpa (Q4FY27, ₹70 cr). Management says there is no further capex in distillation.
**Competition.** Domestic pitch rivals are small (Himadri 65%+), and management says it sells pitch in India below Chinese prices. Carbon black competes with PCBL and global majors.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a good business with scale and integration that newcomers cannot copy quickly. But FY22-26 profit growth came almost entirely from EBITDA per tonne, which is partly cyclical (raw-material spreads). We assume ~₹20,500 per tonne in FY27 (Q1: ~₹23,654 on a consolidated core basis), rising to ~₹21,500 by FY29 with the mix, on volume growth of 6% / 8% / 5%. Core EBITDA: ₹{{F.seg.core.adjEbitda.0|num}} cr / ₹{{F.seg.core.adjEbitda.1|num}} cr / ₹{{F.seg.core.adjEbitda.2|num}} cr (FY26: ₹978 cr).

sections.title: Carbon black: the move to speciality grades is the real story of FY22-26

blocks.p: Carbon black is fine soot made by burning heavy oil in a controlled way; ~90% of the world's output goes into tyres and rubber. Speciality grades (for plastics, masterbatch, inks, coatings, cables and battery electrodes) need tighter control of particle size and purity and sell at higher prices per kilogram, not per tonne. Himadri makes its own feedstock oil from coal tar, which is its edge. It has 250 kt of carbon black capacity, of which 130 kt is speciality after a 70 kt line (₹220 cr) started in FY26, sold under nine brands (Energex and Electra for batteries, Jetex for cables, Klarex and Colorx for plastics and inks, among others). Next: 6,000 tpa of **super speciality black** (₹170 cr, Q4FY28), converted from commodity rubber-black lines, which management says carries margins "significantly higher" than speciality.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the speciality shift is genuine and it is why ICICI Securities saw "EBITDA/kg continues to surprise positively" in 2025. It is also where spreads can compress: in Q3FY26 EBITDA per kilogram dipped as speciality spreads came under pressure (ICICI Securities, Jan-2026). The new 70 kt line is the main volume driver of FY27; super speciality is too small (6 kt) to move group numbers before FY29.

sections.title: Birla Tyres: revenue is coming back, profit is not here yet

blocks.p: Birla Tyres was a well-known bias-tyre brand that went bankrupt. In Oct-2023 Himadri and Dalmia Bharat Refractories (DBRL) won it in insolvency; the plant restarted on 29-May-2025. The structure is complicated: the manufacturing undertaking sits in DBRL, funded by NCDs that Himadri holds (₹487 cr at Mar-26, up from ₹187 cr); Himadri owns the brand company (Birla Tyres Ltd, 100%) and 49%, with control, of the selling company. On 21-Sep-2026 the boards approved a scheme to demerge DBRL's tyre business into HSCL (1 HSCL share per 260 DBRL shares; FY26 turnover of that business ₹149 cr), which would simplify this. The focus is agri, off-the-road (OTR) and truck-bus bias tyres, with a radial car-tyre (PCR) plant for EVs and SUVs planned by FY28.

By FY28 Himadri will have put ~₹1,000 cr (NCDs plus capex) into a business earning perhaps ₹50 cr of EBITDA.

sections.title: Battery materials: a ₹1,245 cr bet on beating China at its own game

blocks.p: Himadri has worked on battery chemistry for over a decade and is building three things. (1) **Anode material** from its own specially engineered pitch: a 200 tpa plant started on 23-Apr-2026 (₹120 cr), revenue potential ₹120-130 cr, samples at stage B of a four-stage approval that takes 1.5-2 years; a commercial-scale plant is still to be announced. (2) **LFP cathode** (lithium iron phosphate, the chemistry of most EV and grid-storage batteries): 2,000 tpa in Q3FY27, then the rest of a 40,000 tpa Phase 1 (₹1,125 cr) over about 12 months, with FY29 the first full year; management says ~₹3,000 cr of revenue at full use, a 2x asset turn, and a long-term goal of 200,000 tpa (₹4,800 cr). It claims to be the first commercial LFP plant outside China. (3) **Partnerships**: a licence for Sicona's silicon-carbon anode (Australia), 19.44% of International Battery Company (US cell maker with a Korean plant and an Indian gigafactory planned for Q4FY27), and 40% of Invati.

blocks.title: Moat scorecard
blocks.source: GAM research compilation (filings and calls to Sep-2026)

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Himadri has a **narrow moat in coal tar processing and pitch**: scale, integration and customer approvals that a new entrant cannot copy quickly, in a market where supply is tied to steel. In carbon black it has a cost edge from its own feedstock but competes with global majors on quality. It has **no moat yet in battery materials or tyres**, where most of the new capital is going. Margins in the core still move with raw-material spreads, as FY21-22 showed.

sections.title: Flat revenue, five-fold profit: FY22-26 was a margin story

blocks.p: Himadri's numbers fall into two eras. Until FY22 it was a coal tar processor with thin, volatile margins: in FY21-22 raw-material costs ran ahead of prices, the EBITDA margin fell to 6% and net profit to ₹39 cr. Since then revenue has gone up only 67% (₹2,791 cr to ₹4,661 cr, and almost flat from FY23 to FY26), but EBITDA rose six-fold and net profit nearly twenty-fold to ₹755 cr. The driver was EBITDA per tonne: about ₹4,400 in FY22, ₹17,300 in FY26 and ~₹23,700 in Q1FY27, as more of the coal tar went into speciality carbon black, high-grade pitch and oils, and costs came down. Q1FY27 revenue rose 28% (₹1,432 cr) and net profit 27% (₹228 cr), the first quarter with real top-line growth.

pair.title: Other income jumped to ₹171 cr in FY26

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the improvement is real and has lasted four years, but it came mostly from margin, not volume (standalone volume +52% since FY22, +2% in FY26). FY26 profit also had help from other income of ₹171 cr, of which ₹100 cr was a fair-value gain on start-up investments. From FY27 growth must come from new capacity: speciality black, pitch exports, anthraquinone, tyres and, later, battery materials.

sections.title: Lean capex until FY25; now the biggest investment cycle in its history

blocks.p: For four years Himadri spent little on plants: capex was ₹23-171 cr a year in FY22-25, so most of the ₹1,619 cr of operating cash in FY22-26 went to paying down debt and building cash. That changed in FY26 (capex ₹450 cr, the 70 kt speciality black line) and changes more in FY27-28: management plans ~₹1,000 cr of capex in each year (LFP ₹1,125 cr, tyres ~₹500 cr, CNT, SSCB, anthraquinone). The other big use of cash has been investments outside the plant: ₹1,029 cr of investments bought in FY24-26, mainly Dalmia Bharat Refractories NCDs that fund the Birla Tyres plant (₹487 cr at Mar-26), IBC, Sicona and mutual funds. Returns are good: Screener ROCE 22%, the company's own figure 32% (it leaves out investments and CWIP).

blocks.callout: **Where it went right and wrong:** the speciality carbon black and pitch investments paid back quickly: EBITDA per tonne quadrupled. The open question is the next ₹2,000 cr. Batteries (₹1,245 cr committed to LFP and anode) have no orders yet, and tyres have absorbed ~₹490 cr of NCD funding plus ~₹500 cr of planned capex for ₹187 cr of FY26 revenue at about break-even. On our numbers ROE slips from 18% to ~16% in FY28E while that capital ramps up.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but other income and cash conversion need watching

bullets: **Forex inside expenses.** The company's EBITDA (₹1,006 cr in FY26) excludes forex; the P&L books forex in other expenses (FY26 loss ₹43.6 cr, Q1FY27 loss ₹25.2 cr). Screener's EBITDA (₹962 cr) is after the loss.

**Other income.** ₹171 cr in FY26 (₹52 cr FY25; ₹56 cr in Q1FY27): interest on deposits partly funded by short-term borrowing (borrowings rose from ₹313 cr to ₹770 cr in FY26), mutual-fund gains and fair-value gains on IBC, Sicona and Birla Tyres instruments. It was 17% of FY26 pre-tax profit.

**Fair-value gains in other income.** Of FY26 other income of ₹171.3 cr, ₹100.0 cr was a fair-value gain on non-current investments carried at fair value through P&L (IBC, Sicona and similar; ₹0.2 cr in FY25); interest on bank deposits was ₹43.5 cr. Excluding the fair-value gain, FY26 pre-tax profit would have been ~10% lower.

**Net cash definition.** Company net cash ₹121 cr at Mar-26 (Q4 call; the Jul-2026 deck shows ₹113 cr), down from ~₹371-392 cr at Mar-25 despite record profit, as capex, strategic investments and working capital absorbed cash.
**Cash conversion.** Screener: cash from operations ₹382 cr in FY26 vs EBITDA ₹962 cr (40%); inventory days rose from 68 to 96.

**Consolidation by control.** Invati (40%) and Himadri Birla Tyre Manufacturer (49%) are consolidated as subsidiaries on contractual control (Ind AS 110), so tyre revenue is consolidated while the tyre plant sits in DBRL until the demerger.

**Related parties.** Himadri carries ₹183 cr of optionally convertible preference shares in Modern Hi-Rise, its own promoter holding company (a 1% non-cumulative instrument from a 2018 amalgamation; the issuer decides on conversion or redemption). Small stakes in group companies Himadri Credit & Finance and Himadri e-Carbon.
**Tyre funding off the operating line.** The Birla Tyres plant is funded through ₹487 cr of DBRL NCDs shown as investments, not capex; the demerger will bring the assets onto Himadri's balance sheet.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The audit (Singhi & Co) is unqualified and segment data reconcile. The amber is for the size of other income (17% of FY26 pre-tax profit, over half of it fair-value gains), cash from operations at only 40% of EBITDA in FY26, a sizeable investment in the promoter's holding company, and tyre funding routed through investments.

sections.title: Net cash, but less of it than the headline suggests

blocks.p: The company reported net cash of ₹121 cr at March 2026 (₹113 cr in the July deck), down from ~₹390 cr a year earlier despite record profit. Screener's cash and investments (₹1,795 cr) less borrowings (₹770 cr) gives ₹1,025 cr, but ~₹860 cr of that is long-term investments that cannot pay for capex: DBRL NCDs and preference shares (the Birla Tyres funding), ₹183 cr of preference shares in the promoter holding company Modern Hi-Rise, and the IBC and Sicona stakes. Borrowings rose from ₹313 cr to ₹770 cr: management uses its bank lines and commercial paper and parks the money in deposits for a spread. Working capital rose too: inventory days went from 68 to 96 in FY26. With ~₹2,000 cr of capex in FY27-28, we expect free cash flow to be negative for two years.

sections.title: Ownership: the Choudhary family holds 52.5%; institutions barely 10%

blocks.p: The Choudhary family owns 52.5% (Jun-2026), mostly through Modern Hi-Rise Pvt Ltd (36.75%) and CMD Anurag Choudhary (8.59%, Mar-2026). Its stake rose from 44.8% in Dec-2023 after it converted 1 cr warrants at ₹316 in Nov-2025; nothing is pledged. Institutions own little: foreign investors 6.8%, insurers 2.05% and mutual funds just 1.26%. Retail investors (4,14,141 shareholders) hold most of the rest, which makes the stock volatile (52-week range ₹438-790).

sections.title: Our forecasts: below management's FY28 goal and a little below the street

blocks.p: We forecast three business lines. The core (pitch, carbon black, chemicals and captive power) is built from volume and EBITDA per tonne; tyres and battery materials have their own revenue and margin paths. Other income falls as cash goes into capex and we assume no repeat of FY26's fair-value gains; capex follows management (~₹1,000 cr in each of FY27 and FY28). Every assumption, with its reasoning, is in the Excel model's Assumptions sheet.

Our revenue is lower too (+24% vs +34.8%), as we assume realisations soften. For FY28 our net profit of ₹{{F.pat.1|num}} cr is ~11% below management's ₹1,100 cr+ goal: reaching it needs EBITDA per tonne near Q1's ~₹23,700 or a faster battery ramp. Our EPS grows ~15% a year over FY26-29E.

sections.title: The street: one institutional broker, at HOLD, with targets chasing the price

blocks.p: Coverage is thin for a ₹34,000 cr company. ICICI Securities is the only institutional broker with a standing call on 30-Sep-2026: HOLD, target ₹720 (17-Jul-2026), raised from ₹550 (Apr) and ₹470 (Jan) as the share price rose; its method is a sum of the parts with the core on FY28E EV/EBITDA (12x in Jan, 15x in Apr; the July multiple is not public). Retail desks are more bullish: Mehta Equities (Feb, ₹571, buy on dips; battery business at 2.2x invested capital, 30x FY27E P/E as a check) and a technical call from IDBI Capital's derivatives desk (Jun, ₹900). The one consensus figure we found (Trendlyne, one analyst) expects FY27 revenue +35% and profit +24%. Bulls point to the speciality mix and the battery option; the brokers' own caution is about valuation and the battery timeline.

sections.title: Valuation: 25x Sep-28E earnings gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}

blocks.h: How the street values Himadri Speciality Chemical

blocks.p: Only one institutional broker covers Himadri: **ICICI Securities values it on a sum of the parts, with the core business on FY28E EV/EBITDA** (12x in Jan-2026, 15x in Apr-2026; the July multiple behind its ₹720 target is not public). We use **P/E** instead, for four reasons: Himadri has net cash and little interest, so for the core EV/EBITDA and P/E carry the same information; ICICI's other parts (tyres, batteries, investments) are not disclosed, so we cannot copy them; management sets its goal in profit (₹1,100 cr+ PAT in FY28); and retail brokers use P/E. Our EV/EBITDA cross-check replicates ICICI's core method. We apply the multiple to the earnings the market will look at in September 2027 (Sep-28E: half FY28E, half FY29E).

sections.title: Our honest summary: a better business than it was, at a price that assumes it keeps getting better

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's dominant coal tar pitch and naphthalene maker, with a fast-growing speciality carbon black arm, a debt-free balance sheet and ~18% ROE; plus two early bets, battery materials (LFP and anode) and a revived tyre brand, that will absorb most of the next ₹2,000 cr of capex.

**What you are paying:** 35.2x our FY28E EPS and 32.4x Sep-28E, against a forward median of ~25x since 2021, for EPS growth of ~15% a year once margins normalise. On P/E and our inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}); ICICI Securities' EV/EBITDA approach on our numbers lands slightly lower, and the DCF lower still.

bullets: **Rating: SELL, target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).** Our ratings follow the upside to our 12−month target: BUY at +15% or more, HOLD between −5% and +15%, SELL below −5%.
**We would move to HOLD if the price fell below ~₹550 and to BUY below ~₹450**, or sooner if EBITDA per tonne proves sustainable near Q1FY27's level (our bull case) or LFP wins named orders.
**Biggest swing factor:** core EBITDA per tonne. Our base case assumes it eases from ~₹23,700 in Q1FY27 to ~₹20,500 for FY27; holding the Q1 level would add ~13% to FY28E EPS.

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: A thick liquid by-product of turning coal into coke for steel-making; Himadri's main raw material.
The solid or liquid residue of distilling coal tar; binds the carbon anodes in aluminium smelters and graphite electrodes.
Fine carbon powder made by burning heavy oil; reinforces tyres and rubber. Speciality grades colour and conduct in plastics, inks, cables and batteries.
Super speciality carbon black (high-purity niche grades) and carbon nanotubes (rolled graphene, used as conductive additives in batteries and electronics).
A coal tar fraction used for phthalic anhydride, dyes and mothballs; SNF (sulphonated naphthalene formaldehyde) is a concrete admixture.
Speciality chemicals from coal tar used in dyes, hydrogen peroxide, pharma and electronics; India imports them today.
Lithium iron phosphate, the positive-electrode powder in most EV and storage batteries; the anode is the negative electrode, usually graphite.
Operating profit before depreciation divided by tonnes sold; our main measure of the core's profitability.
Off-the-road tyres (mining, construction), passenger-car radial tyres, truck-bus bias tyres.
Sum of the parts: valuing each business separately and adding them up.
Share price ÷ earnings per share; enterprise value (market value plus net debt) ÷ operating profit before depreciation.
Profit as % of shareholders' equity / operating profit as % of capital employed.
Discounted cash flow valuation; WACC is the blended required return used to discount future cash.
